subject: Biology
title: Plant Growth and Development
summary: Growth is an irreversible permanent increase in size. In plants it is indeterminate (open) because meristems keep dividing. It has three phases — meristematic, elongation and maturation — and follows a sigmoid curve.
Growth rate can be arithmetic (one daughter cell keeps dividing) or geometric (both daughter cells divide); differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation shape the plant.
Five plant growth regulators control growth: auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins (promoters), abscisic acid and ethylene (mainly inhibitors).
Development is also controlled by photoperiodism (day length) and vernalisation (low temperature) for flowering, and by seed dormancy.

formulas.name: Arithmetic growth
formulas.when: Linear growth — root elongating at a constant rate.
formulas.note: Gives a straight line when length is plotted against time.

formulas.name: Geometric growth
formulas.formula: Wₜ = W₀ eʳᵗ  (r = relative growth rate, e = 2.718)
formulas.when: Exponential phase of growth (Wₜ final size, W₀ initial size).

formulas.name: Absolute vs relative growth
formulas.formula: absolute = growth per unit time;  relative = growth per unit time per unit initial size

formulas.name: Sigmoid growth curve
formulas.formula: lag phase → log (exponential) phase → stationary phase
formulas.when: Growth of cells, organs or organisms in a limited environment.

formulas.name: Auxins
formulas.formula: IAA, IBA (natural); NAA, 2,4-D (synthetic);  apical dominance, rooting of cuttings, parthenocarpy (tomato), prevent premature leaf and fruit drop, xylem differentiation;  2,4-D kills dicot weeds
formulas.when: Auxin functions (F.W. Went, from Avena coleoptile tips).

formulas.name: Gibberellins
formulas.formula: GA₃ most common (from Gibberella fujikuroi — bakanae disease of rice);  stem elongation (sugarcane yield up by ~20 t/acre), bolting in cabbage/beet, fruit size (grapes), malting (brewing), seed germination, delayed senescence

formulas.name: Cytokinins
formulas.formula: kinetin (from autoclaved herring sperm DNA), zeatin (corn kernels, coconut milk);  cell division, new leaves and chloroplasts, lateral shoot growth (overcomes apical dominance), delay leaf senescence (Richmond–Lang effect)

formulas.name: Ethylene
formulas.formula: gaseous; ripening of fruits (climacteric rise in respiration), triple response in seedlings, horizontal growth, abscission, flowering in pineapple, breaks dormancy;  ethephon releases ethylene
formulas.note: Ethylene is the most widely used PGR in agriculture.

formulas.name: Abscisic acid (ABA)
formulas.formula: stress hormone;  closes stomata, induces dormancy in seeds and buds, promotes abscission;  antagonist of GA

formulas.name: Photoperiodism
formulas.formula: short-day plants flower when days are shorter than a critical length (actually need a long uninterrupted dark period);  long-day plants flower when days are longer;  day-neutral plants are unaffected;  leaves perceive the light
formulas.when: Day-length control of flowering (Garner and Allard).

formulas.name: Vernalisation
formulas.formula: cold treatment needed to promote flowering in some plants — winter wheat, biennials (carrot, sugarbeet, cabbage)

formulas.name: Seed dormancy
formulas.formula: caused by hard seed coat, chemical inhibitors (ABA, phenolics) or immature embryo;  broken by scarification, GA₃, nitrates, chilling

examples.title: Geometric growth
examples.problem: A seedling of 5 g grows with relative growth rate r = 0.1 per day. Mass after 10 days (Wₜ = W₀eʳᵗ)?

examples.title: Relative growth
examples.problem: A leaf grows from 10 cm² to 15 cm². Relative growth (%)?

examples.title: Bolting
examples.problem: Which hormone promotes bolting in cabbage, and what is bolting?
examples.solution: Gibberellin. Bolting is rapid internode elongation just before flowering in rosette plants like cabbage and beet.

examples.title: Apical dominance
examples.problem: Removing the shoot tip makes a plant bushy. Why?
examples.solution: The apical bud makes auxin that suppresses lateral buds (apical dominance). Removing it (decapitation) lets the lateral buds grow — used in tea plantations and hedge-making.

examples.title: Stress hormone
examples.problem: Why is ABA called a stress hormone?
examples.solution: It increases plant tolerance to stresses — it closes stomata during water shortage, induces dormancy to survive bad seasons and inhibits growth.

examples.title: Fruit ripening
examples.problem: Which hormone hastens fruit ripening, and how is it supplied commercially?
examples.solution: Ethylene; it is supplied as ethephon, which releases ethylene in plant tissues. It also promotes female flowers in cucumbers.

topics.title: Plasticity
topics.explain: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different structures — e.g. heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur (different leaves in juvenile and mature plants) and in buttercup (different leaves in air and water).

topics.title: Differentiation, dedifferentiation, redifferentiation
topics.explain: Cells from meristems mature to perform specific functions (differentiation). Living differentiated cells can regain the ability to divide (dedifferentiation — e.g. interfascicular cambium, cork cambium) and then form cells that again lose the ability to divide (redifferentiation).

topics.title: Conditions for growth
topics.explain: Water (for cell enlargement and enzymatic activity), oxygen (for metabolic energy), nutrients, and optimum temperature and light.

topics.title: Discovery of PGRs
topics.explain: Charles and Francis Darwin observed coleoptiles bending towards light (phototropism); F.W. Went isolated auxin from Avena coleoptile tips; E. Kurosawa found gibberellins from a fungus causing bakanae disease; Skoog and Miller found kinetin; ABA was discovered as inhibitor-B, abscisin II and dormin; Cousins confirmed ethylene from ripened oranges.

topics.title: PGR interactions
topics.explain: Hormones act together, sometimes synergistically and sometimes antagonistically — e.g. auxin–cytokinin ratio decides root vs shoot formation in tissue culture; GA and ABA have opposite effects on seed dormancy.

topics.title: Seed germination
topics.explain: When conditions are favourable, seeds absorb water, enzymes are activated and the embryo grows into a seedling. Dormancy prevents germination even under favourable conditions.

ratta: Arithmetic Lₜ = L₀ + rt;  geometric Wₜ = W₀eʳᵗ.
